candidates.title: Stored PRT player reopens an epoch directory without checking that it starts from the checkpoint it is given: state.json does not record the epoch's initial machine, and an existing next-epoch checkpoint is kept without checking it
candidates.component: PRT player in doc/recipes (prt.lua stored player: store_epoch_state, reopen_epoch_directory, new_stored_player, store_next_epoch_checkpoint, store_first_epoch_checkpoint, load_epoch_checkpoint) with crisium.lua (new_player / open_epochs)
candidates.role: Support (AUDIT.md: 'The PRT player and bridge in doc/recipes ... Support. No production deployment runs the player'). It stands in for the honest operator's 'Storing and reloading the machine' and 'Restarting after a stop'.
candidates.location: doc/recipes/prt.lua store_epoch_state (~2602-2647: state.json has initial_outputs_merkle_root but no initial state hash or geometry), reopen_epoch_directory (~3066-3075: the only binding check is the outputs root), new_stored_player (~3197-3205: reopen is chosen whenever state.json exists), store_next_epoch_checkpoint (~2704-2707) and store_first_epoch_checkpoint (~2743-2746: an existing directory is returned unchecked), load_epoch_checkpoint (~3226-3242: geometry and final_state_hash taken from the unhashed epoch.json); doc/recipes/crisium.lua new_player (~172-179) and open_epochs (~224-268: state/epoch-N is named by epoch number only).
candidates.description: Each stored epoch directory is tied to the machine it starts from only by name. state.json records input_count, root_hash, files and initial_outputs_merkle_root, but neither the initial state hash it was cloned from (dapp_contract.initial_state_hash, the checkpoint's final_state_hash) nor the geometry. On a relaunch, new_stored_player reopens any state/epoch-N that has a state.json. reopen_epoch_directory only checks that the stored outputs root equals the checkpoint frontier's root, which is the empty-tree root for every epoch before the first output, and that the epoch machine matches state.json's own root_hash. So a directory that continues a different initial machine (another checkpoint, another application, or another geometry) is adopted silently, and its mcycle claim and proofs are built from that machine. The same holds the other way. store_next_epoch_checkpoint and store_first_epoch_checkpoint return early when the target checkpoint exists, without comparing its epoch.json final_state_hash, input_count and geometry with the sealing player's. load_epoch_checkpoint then trusts epoch.json's log2_mcycles_per_period, which no one compares with the factory geometry that crisium reads and passes to the bridge. The listener's seal check (EpochSealed.initialMachineStateHash == checkpoint hash) checks the checkpoint, not the epoch directory the player actually computes from. Invariant broken: 'the recorded hashes always describe the directory next to them', and 'the next epoch starts from the previous epoch's final machine', in the form 'the epoch directory a player reopens continues the checkpoint it was given'.
candidates.trigger: The operator (trusted caller) relaunches crisium with a --state directory holding epoch-N from another deployment, application or checkpoint set: a redeployment that reuses --state, or a checkpoints directory that is restored or regenerated (for example, epoch-0 rebuilt from another template while players/honest/epoch-0 is kept). No adversary action is needed or possible. A reorg past the input policy (out of scope) can also leave a checkpoint that store_next_epoch_checkpoint then keeps.
candidates.reachability: The guest cannot reach it. Within one deployment and without operator error, the code keeps the pair consistent: a checkpoint is written only once per seal and atomically renamed, and remove_epoch_files removes checkpoint K together with state/epoch-K. So in-scope runs never produce the mismatch. It needs operator misuse of its own records or an out-of-scope reorg.
candidates.rating_steps: 1. Out of scope? A stale checkpoint left by a reorg deeper than the input policy is excluded ('Reorganizations of the chain deeper than the operator's input policy'). The operator-reuse trigger is not in the out-of-scope list. 2. Role: the stored PRT player is Support per AUDIT.md. 3. High/Medium cases: none fits. It is not 'A machine API operation off the honest operator's path that, used as documented, leaves ... a stored directory inconsistent', since the player's records are not machine API state, and the trigger is misuse, not documented use. 4. Critical: no rule is violated on the honest operator's path when the operator uses its own records as documented. O2 ('resume only from a guaranteed directory') is met literally: the directory is guaranteed, just for another epoch lineage. 5. Low: 'a failure that needs misuse of an API by its trusted caller'. Low, as defense-in-depth. If triage reads the relaunch with the documented --state layout as part of 'Restarting after a stop' (R4: 'After a stop, it restarts from a directory that O2 guarantees and keeps defending its claim'), the stood-in honest-operator defect would be Critical, so Medium for Support. The deciding fact is whether reusing a --state directory across deployments or checkpoint sets counts as documented use.
candidates.threat_to_goal: If it happens, the honest player defends a claim computed from the wrong initial machine (or geometry), loses every match, and a dishonest claim can settle, which is a completeness failure of section 1. Nothing in the player detects it, except an outputs-root mismatch once outputs exist.
candidates.evidence: Code reading only for this candidate. There is no check of dapp_contract.initial_state_hash or geometry anywhere in reopen_epoch_directory, and no initial-hash field in EPOCH_STATE_SCHEMAS/state.json. A related experiment (below, in not_covered) showed that reopen after SIGKILL at 5 points reproduces identical answers, so the in-scope restart paths are consistent.
candidates.test_idea: Store template A and template B, both genesis templates with an empty outputs root. Run prt.new_stored_player(dapp_A, ..., E) for one input and close it. Then call prt.new_stored_player(dapp_B, ..., E) with the same epoch directory E and assert that it raises an error (the required behavior: refuse an epoch directory that does not continue dapp_B.initial_state_hash). Today it reopens and commit_mcycle_claim returns A's claim. Likewise, call store_first_epoch_checkpoint(B, ...) on an existing checkpoint made from A and assert that it raises an error instead of keeping A.

not_covered: Power-loss (unsynced page cache) injection. Only SIGKILL was exercised. Earlier candidates R1-O2-1 and R1-O2-2 cover the known power-loss windows of reopen. By reading, every other commit point (entries, forests, frontier files, machine-cache files, last-output files, state.json, checkpoint rename, remove_stored) syncs before the next commit point relies on it.

The full crisium process (listeners, bridge, keep_epochs removal, .removed completion) on the local chain and the player-restart runner were not run. crisium's epoch opening and removal ordering was checked by reading only.

Kills during bundle expansion (store_expansion of an opened bundle) and inside a uarch claim build were not injected. Kills tested: inside a rejected input after remove_stored(machine) (clone_stored #7), inside the agreed pair's rejected-input revert (clone_stored #22), at the seal before the checkpoint rename (rename_stored #1), after the sealed state.json before machine.revert removal (remove_stored #15), and at remove_evicted after state.json (remove_stored #6). In all 5 cases, reopening and finishing gave the same answers as the uninterrupted baseline: the mcycle claim, a reveal_bisection, 16 prove_state_transition logs, the uarch claim, the outputs-root proof, the final hash and the checkpoint epoch.json. The script is SUBEPOCHDIR/exp.lua with run.sh (bare-metal emit-output guest, inputs a1,R,b22,c333,R,d4,e5,R, and a copy of prt.lua with STORED_MACHINE_CACHE_CAPACITY=3 so that the agreed pair advances from entry 4 to 7 across a rejected input). The baseline with capacity 32 gave identical answers.

The stored versus forked player differential. I compared the stored player against itself across cache capacities 32 and 3 (the second makes the agreed pair advance across a rejected input) and across kills, not against the forked player or a naive reference.

Epochs that stop (halt, exception yield, imcyclemax) were not exercised with the stored player, by reading only. I argued the 'halted with a rejected tohost and iflags_Y' state behind get_mcycle_sample_hash to be unreachable, since a manual yield stops the machine before any halt can be written, but did not test it.

R12 cost of the per-input stored commit (full clone without reflinks, about 35 MB per clone here) and of restarts. Not measured. The experiment showed about 25 s per input on ext4 with discard, which A7 sizing would decide.
Hash-tree internals of forest stores (merge_node and the rewrite of trees with another representation) beyond their use by the player.
The sentinel's own checkpoints and adversary kinds (out of scope).
